builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MaskPE: One Mask, Two Roles: Weight Placement and MAC Gating in Systolic Arrays
summary: MaskPE replaces conventional weight-stationary systolic PE placement and zero-skipping logic with mask-directed weight preloading and clock gating of arithmetic registers in zero-weight PEs. The cost is custom hardware: positional mask metadata, RTL redesign, and per-tile mask steering, with gains validated only at gate level rather than on silicon. For the reader it can simply fail to apply at all, since its energy and storage benefits exist only on custom accelerators, not on GPUs or third-party APIs.
rationale: The method is a custom systolic-array RTL design requiring silicon or FPGA implementation, which a GPU/API-constrained practitioner cannot deploy; it is relevant only as context for how sparsity becomes real savings on future hardware.
technique: Mask-directed systolic PE gating for sparsity

claims.statement: MaskPE replaces conventional weight-stationary systolic PE placement and zero-skipping logic with mask-directed weight preloading and clock gating of arithmetic registers in zero-weight PEs. The cost is custom hardware: positional mask metadata, RTL redesign, and per-tile mask steering, with gains validated only at gate level rather than on silicon. For the reader it can simply fail to apply at all, since its energy and storage benefits exist only on custom accelerators, not on GPUs or third-party APIs.
At 50% sparsity, 34.9% lower compressed weight storage including metadata, and 12.5--14.4% lower execution energy across seven LLM projections in gate-level simulation.
